specification.problem: Optimal discrimination of group translates of a state under a unitary representation of a finite group, applied to GROUP MULTIPLICATION for two elements with one quantum query (success probability 2/|G|, generalizing Deutsch's algorithm).
specification.reconstruction_scope: Tiny instance: the generic optimal state-discrimination formulation for a group representation, plus the abstract's stated success probability 2/|G| for the two-element product. Group G=Z_2 is used as a sanity check where 2/|G|=1 (Deutsch). The explicit optimal state, query oracle construction, and the Hidden Conjugating Element algorithm are outside scope.

symbols.meaning: state whose translates are to be distinguished
probability of correctly identifying the group element applied

equations.label: Translate family
equations.description: Set of translates of the state under the group; the task is to choose |psi> maximizing the probability of distinguishing them.
equations.abstract_quote: find a state whose translates under the group are distinguishable with the highest probability
equations.justification: Directly describes the family of states being discriminated.

equations.label: Optimal discrimination objective
equations.description: Maximum success probability over states and POVMs under a uniform prior.
equations.justification: Standard minimum-error discrimination formulation; the paper's actual solution method is not given in the abstract.

equations.label: Two-element product success probability
equations.description: Success probability of the single-query algorithm for the product of two elements of G; stated as optimal.
equations.abstract_quote: we give an algorithm to find the product of two elements of $G$ with a single quantum query with probability $2/|G|$

equations.label: Deutsch special case
equations.description: For Z_2 the formula gives certainty, consistent with Deutsch's algorithm.
equations.abstract_quote: This generalizes Deutsch’s Algorithm from $\hbox{\bbb Z}_{2}$ to an arbitrary finite group.

equations.label: Hidden conjugating element oracle
equations.latex: O_a:\ x\mapsto a x a^{-1},\ a\in G\text{ unknown}
equations.description: Oracle acts by conjugation by an unknown element a; the goal is to determine a.
equations.abstract_quote: the oracle acts by conjugating by an unknown element of the group
equations.justification: Formal reading of the verbal description; the quantum implementation is not specified. Note that a is determined only up to the center of G by conjugation alone, a caveat not discussed in the abstract.
assumptions: Classical action written as x -> a x a^{-1}

registers.name: R
registers.role: Register holding the probe state in representation space H; the query oracle encoding is not specified in the abstract.

specification.initial_state: An optimal state |psi> in H maximizing discrimination of its translates; its explicit form is not given in the abstract.

steps.description: Choose a representation rho of G on H and find a state |psi> maximizing the translate-discrimination success probability.
For the two-element product problem, use a single query and discriminate to obtain the product with probability 2/|G|.
For the hidden conjugating element problem, apply the oracle once to the probe state and discriminate the resulting states.

specification.measurement: Optimal discriminating POVM {E_g} on the translated states; its explicit form is not given in the abstract.
assumptions: Minimum-error discrimination as the figure of merit
Z_2 used as the tiny sanity instance
